Duties and Role

Introduction

The NATO Cyber and Digital Transformation (CDT) division drives NATO's Digital Transformation, including the secure adoption, integration, and operational use of emerging digital technologies across the NATO Enterprise. As Artificial Intelligence capabilities become increasingly embedded in NATO systems, services, decision-support capabilities, and security-enforcing technologies, NATO must ensure that AI-related cyber security risks are identified, assessed, and addressed through clear, comprehensive, mandatory, and implementable technical security requirements.
As a result, this post will be focused on supporting NATO in the assessment, development, validation, and coordination of technical and implementation security requirements needed to address prominent AI-related CIS/cyber security risks to NATO. These risks include, but are not limited to:

  • The offensive use of AI against NATO systems, services, data, networks, users, and missions;
  • The secure use of AI capabilities in classified environments; and
  • The embedding of AI into security-enforcing products, services, capabilities, and architectures.

The contractor will provide expert support to identify AI-related cyber security risks, translate them into actionable and testable automated security requirements, and support their coordination with relevant NATO stakeholders, governance bodies, technical communities, capability programmes, and implementation authorities.

Tasks

The division requires a professional who can provide expert support in the analysis, coordination, development, validation, and maintenance of mandatory CIS security technical and implementation requirements addressing AI-related cyber security risks to NATO.

The contractor shall support CDT and relevant NATO stakeholders in developing requirements that are clear, actionable, measurable, testable, technically feasible, and suitable for inclusion in NATO security directives, implementation guidance, acquisition requirements, accreditation artefacts, capability development documentation, reference architectures, and/or other applicable NATO governance or engineering products.

Location of Duty

The contractor will be embedded within CDT, working in the Interoperability and Standardization Section (ISS), within the Strategy and Policy Directorate, and in coordination with the NATO Communication and Information Agency (NCIA), the NATO Office of Security (NOS), Capability Panels, and other stakeholders. The duty location is in NATO HQ in Brussels, Belgium.

The contractor is expected to work 5 days a week on site and may perform in specific (but very limited in frequency) situations teleworking at his residence in Belgium, following a security assessment of the place. No teleworking is allowed outside of the respective residence in Belgium.

Requirements

  • NATO Secret security clearance
  • The candidate must possess a university degree in a relevant engineering or technical field such as computer science, systems science, or an equivalent technical qualification;
  • The candidate must have comprehensive knowledge of the principles of computer and communications security, networking, and the vulnerabilities of modern operating systems and applications;
  • The candidate must have at least five (5) years of demonstrated experience working with national or international CIS and cyber security standards, including their application and auditing at both governance and operational levels. Demonstrated experience working with MITRE ATLAS, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, CSA STAR for AI, or similar, is essential;
  • The candidate must have demonstrated experience in the field of Artificial Intelligence, its security benefits and associated risks;
  • The candidate must have proven knowledge of securing AI-enabled systems and data-driven capabilities;
  • The candidate must have demonstrated experience in defining and implementing cyber security architectures, including Zero Trust principles;
  • The candidate must have basic knowledge of high-level programming languages. Experience with languages such as Python is desirable;
  • The candidate must demonstrate strong communication and presentation skills, including the ability to convey complex cyber security concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences;
  • The candidate must demonstrate strong project management skills;
